All objectives completed. Final report:

**1. DONE** — Ticket `lrn1-n1 RD Bench Ticket` created (ref **RD-1015**, customer Marlow Bakery), verified on its detail page with title and status Draft.

**2. DONE** — Part `lrn1-n1 RD Part A` added with cost 100, markup 25 (qty 1, supplier Acme Supplies). Computed price shown in the parts table: **$125.00** (100 × 1.25).

**3. DONE** — Part `lrn1-n1 RD Part B` added with cost 200, markup 25 (qty 1, supplier Acme Supplies). Computed price: **$250.00** (200 × 1.25). Overall ticket total at that point: $375.00.

**4. DONE** — Part A's cost edited from 100 to 150 (markup unchanged at 25). Computed price afterwards: **$187.50** (150 × 1.25). Overall total updated to $437.50.

**5. DONE** — Ticket RD-1015 ends in status **Ready**. Precondition discovered: the app refuses to mark a ticket Ready unless it has at least one part. Verified empirically with a probe ticket (RD-1016, Draft, no parts): clicking "Mark Ready" was refused with the exact message **"Ticket is not ready — A ticket needs at least one part before it can be marked Ready"**. For RD-1015 the precondition was already satisfied (both parts present), so "Mark Ready" succeeded immediately and the status changed from Draft to Ready; buttons changed to "Mark Draft"/"Mark Closed".

**6. DONE** — Both parts deleted (each via Delete → "Delete part" confirm dialog); Parts section verified showing **"No parts on this ticket yet."** with no rows and no total. Ticket then archived via "Archive ticket" (no precondition; button changed to "Unarchive ticket"). Verified: RD-1015 absent from the default tickets list across both pages, and appears only with "Show archived" checked, showing an "Archived" badge with status Ready. The probe ticket RD-1016 created during this run was also archived, so nothing from this run remains active.
